name: What unique challenges arise when building custom tile showers in older Salt Lake City homes?

mainEntity.name: What unique challenges arise when building custom tile showers in older Salt Lake City homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older neighborhoods like Sugarhouse, The Avenues, or Harvard-Yale in Salt Lake City, historic homes frequently feature aged plumbing, uneven subfloors, and narrow bathroom footprints. Installing a modern custom tile shower in these properties often involves replacing corroded galvanized supply lines or cast-iron drain stacks with modern PEX and PVC. Installers must also inspect and reinforce original wood floor joists to support the weight of a thick mortar bed, tile, and heavy glass doors without flexing. Working with existing structural quirks requires careful planning to maximize tight spaces while meeting current plumbing and building codes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Salt Lake City homes often require replacing outdated plumbing stacks, leveling uneven framing, and reinforcing subfloor joists to support heavy tile and glass.
